source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Organic Evolution
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: In the Miller–Urey spark-discharge experiment the simulated atmosphere included
options: methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour
questions.explanation: Miller passed sparks through a reducing mix of CH4, NH3, H2 and steam and recovered amino acids.

questions.stem: Lamarck's idea that organs used become stronger and unused ones weaken is called
questions.explanation: Use and disuse, plus inheritance of the resulting acquired characters, is the core of Lamarckism.

questions.stem: According to Darwin, populations become better matched to their environment mainly by
questions.explanation: Individuals with heritable advantages leave more offspring, so adaptive traits increase.

questions.stem: Hugo de Vries proposed that new species can arise suddenly through
questions.explanation: De Vries, working on evening primrose, treated large mutations as the origin of species.

questions.stem: Homologous organs are taken as evidence of
options: common ancestry even if functions differ
identical function with no shared origin
questions.explanation: Similar plan and embryonic origin (for example pentadactyl limbs) indicate divergence from a common ancestor.

questions.stem: Wings of a butterfly and a bird are classified as
questions.explanation: They serve flight but arise from different structures, a case of analogy.

questions.stem: Archaeopteryx is treated as a connecting link between
questions.explanation: It combined feathers and wings with teeth, a long tail and claws on the forelimb.

questions.stem: For a two-allele autosomal locus in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, allele frequencies satisfy
questions.explanation: The two alleles exhaust the gene pool, so their frequencies sum to one; genotypes are p², 2pq and q².

questions.stem: Origin of new species after a geographic barrier splits a population is called
questions.explanation: Physical isolation allows independent genetic change until reproductive isolation is complete.

questions.stem: Darwin's finches of the Galápagos Islands are a textbook case of
questions.explanation: One ancestral stock diversified into many beak types occupying different niches.

questions.stem: Oparin and Haldane independently suggested that life began in a
questions.explanation: A reducing mix allowed abiotic synthesis of organic monomers that accumulated in a 'soup'.

questions.stem: Which claim would Lamarck have accepted but modern genetics rejects?
questions.explanation: Stretching or use during an individual's life does not rewrite the germline DNA passed to offspring.

questions.stem: If q squared equals 0.16 for an autosomal recessive trait at equilibrium, the frequency of heterozygotes is
Amino acids appeared in Miller's apparatus because the experimental atmosphere lacked
questions.explanation: Free O2 would have oxidised precursors; the classic mix was reducing (CH4, NH3, H2, steam).

questions.stem: Explaining a giraffe's long neck by stretching during life and then passing that length to offspring is
questions.explanation: Inheritance of acquired characters is Lamarck's mechanism, not selection among heritable variants.

questions.stem: Industrial melanism in Biston betularia is cited as field evidence for
options: de Vries saltation as the only cause
questions.explanation: Dark moths were better camouflaged on sooty bark and increased under selection by birds.

questions.stem: The modern synthetic theory of evolution combines Darwinian selection with
questions.explanation: Neo-Darwinism treats mutation, recombination, selection, drift and isolation as joint causes.

questions.stem: Forelimbs of whale, bat and cheetah share a pentadactyl skeleton and are therefore
questions.explanation: The same bone plan modified for swimming, flying and running is homology (divergent evolution).

questions.stem: Analogous organs arise mainly through
options: divergent evolution of one ancestral organ
questions.explanation: Unrelated lineages facing similar demands evolve similar functions from different origins.

questions.stem: The human vermiform appendix is commonly cited as a
questions.explanation: It is a reduced remnant of a larger caecum and has no essential digestive role in humans.

questions.stem: Random mating in a very large population with no selection, mutation or migration tends to keep
options: only dominant alleles in the pool
questions.explanation: Those are the Hardy–Weinberg conditions under which p and q do not change.

questions.stem: Reproductive isolation is essential for the
options: industrial melanism of a single gene pool
questions.explanation: Once gene flow is blocked, diverging populations become separate biological species.

questions.stem: Australopithecus is placed on the human evolutionary line mainly because it
options: walked upright and had a larger brain than contemporary apes
questions.explanation: Bipedal australopithecines are early hominins connecting ape-like ancestors to later Homo.

questions.stem: According to Oparin, the atmosphere of primitive Earth was
questions.explanation: A reducing mix of hydrogen-rich gases was postulated to allow abiotic organic synthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a tenet of Lamarckism?
options: survival of the fittest among preexisting heritable variants
an inner vital force driving greater complexity
questions.explanation: Differential survival of preexisting variants is Darwinian; Lamarck invoked use, disuse and acquired inheritance.

questions.stem: Random change of allele frequencies is strongest in
options: clones that have no genetic variation
ideal Hardy–Weinberg populations of infinite size
questions.explanation: Genetic drift (sampling error) has large effects when N is small.
